title.narrative: Grievances responded to within stipulated time

comment.narrative: Only one feedback form has been registered by the team since the Project became effective, mostly due to the delayed commencement of works, expected to start at the end of 2023. The advancement of technical designs during 2022 and the process of consultations have promoted the availability of feedback channels for the project. Also, given the low intake of grievances on other WB projects in Romania, several measures have been designed to engage directly with neighbors in different project phases, such as handling invitations in person, distributing leaflets and posters in the area, and inviting local authorities and organizations to the public consultations. Public consultations for Bucharest Precinct 14 was also an opportunity to create engagement with the immediate community of the station, as several neighbors wanted to discuss in detail about the limitations to access their parking lots during construction works. Several meetings were held and a protocol was signed between the Project and the owner and resident association of one of the neighboring blocks.

title.narrative: Share of trained Police personnel with newly acquired skills and emergency response equipment participating in operational interventions

comment.narrative: In 2025â€“2026, the Project aims to train most personnel with access to emergency response equipment, as well as regular police staff. So far, 81 officers have been trained, with at least 150 expected to be trained by year-endâ€”mostly those using emergency equipment. While a percentage cannot yet be estimated due to variable staff availability, it is notable that around 98% of those equipped have already been trained in its use.

title.narrative: Communities reached through informative community meetings

comment.narrative:
The advancement of the technical designs for the buildings under batch 1 has created the opportunity to engage with the direct beneficiaries, the staff of these units, as well as neighbors, close-by institutions and businesses, local authorities and the general population living in the area of the sub-projects. The consultations on the design have been coupled with the consultation of the ESMPs, and have included several actions, such as: in-person handing of the invitations to the consultation for immediate neighbors, direct meetings with potentially affected stakeholders (schools, nurseries, neighbors), posters displayed at the level of multi-apartment block buildings, invitations sent to owner and resident associations, local NGOS, local authorities by email, handling of feedback forms and info notes on project and Environmental and Social implications together with the invitations, and one public consultation session.
The potentially affected parties (such as relocated staff, immediate neighbors, sensitive institutions such as schools and nurseries) will be visited at the commencement of works and during demolition and constructions works and will have a grievance box available on the site, as well as all available channels of the GRM that were made available during consultations (a dedicated GRM board will be installed next to the grievance box).
Following the example from the similar DRM projects in Romania, the inauguration of the police units, once finalized, will be an opportunity to organize community events, where staff and their families, neighbors, and interested community members can participate at the event and find out more about the overall purpose of the project to support disaster risk management.
The citizen perception survey that will reach out to local communities in the settlements that are undergoing investments will be a great opportunity to better understand the perceived role of the Police in emergency and disaster response.
Retrofitting or reconstruction designs completed for disaster and emergency response facilities.
The target has already been achieved
